slides.say: The fourth one is circle, triangle, circle. Again, the triangle must be equilateral. A circle around the triangle, with its three corners on the circle. And a circle inside the triangle, touching all three sides. Both circles have the same center, O.
at: with its three corners on the circle

slides.say: Here the big radius is twice the small radius. Let's see why. Draw the small radius r, from O to M, the point where the small circle touches the bottom side. A radius to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the side. So there's a right angle at M.
Now draw the big radius R, from O to the corner C. We get the right triangle O M C.
at: Now draw the big radius R

slides.say: The angle at C is half of the triangle's sixty degrees, so it's thirty. Why half? Because the equilateral triangle is symmetric, so the line from the corner C to the center cuts that corner's angle into two equal halves. So O M C is a gold triangle, thirty, sixty, ninety.
In a gold triangle, the side across from the thirty is half of the hypotenuse. Here the side across from the thirty is r, and the hypotenuse is big R. So r is half of big R, and big R is two times r.
at: So r is half of big R
big R is two times r

slides.say: The gold triangle also gives us the side. The long leg, M C, is r root three. M is the middle of the side B C, so the whole side is two r root three. And two r is big R, so the side is big R root three.
at: so the whole side is two r root three
so the side is big R root three

slides.say: Let's try it in numbers. Say the small radius is three. The big radius is twice that, six. The small circle's area is pi times three squared, nine pi. The big circle's area is pi times six squared, thirty-six pi.
at: Say the small radius is three
The big radius is twice that

slides.say: Thirty-six pi is four times nine pi. So the big circle's area is four times the small circle's area. That's the scaling rule again. Every length is multiplied by two, so the area is multiplied by two squared, four.
at: So the big circle's area is four times

slides.say: Questions like to ask about the ring, the part between the two circles. The ring is the big circle minus the small one. Thirty-six pi minus nine pi is twenty-seven pi. And twenty-seven pi is three times nine pi. So the ring is three small circles.
at: Questions like to ask about the ring
twenty-seven pi is three times nine pi

slides.say: And the triangle's side is big R root three. Here big R is six, so the side is six root three.
at: so the side is six root three
so the side is six root three

slides.say: The ring's area is three times the small circle's area, whatever the radius. Let's try a small radius of two. The big radius is four. Its area is pi times four squared, sixteen pi. The small circle's area is pi times two squared, four pi. Sixteen pi minus four pi leaves twelve pi for the ring. Twelve pi is three times four pi, so the same area ratio holds.
at: Let's try a small radius of two
Twelve pi is three times four pi

slides.say: Now, this is important. A length factor isn't an area factor. The area factor is the length factor, squared.
at: The area factor is the length factor

slides.say: In the first two arrangements, every length is multiplied by root two. So the areas are multiplied by two. In the two triangle arrangements, every length is multiplied by two. So the areas are multiplied by four.
at: So the areas are multiplied by two
every length is multiplied by two
So the areas are multiplied by four

slides.say: So remember the four area ratios, the outer area over the inner area. They are two, two, four and four. Take a moment to memorize this, and I'll see you in the next video.
at: the outer area over the inner area
